steps.calloutTitle: First Bank of Nepal — financed emissions
steps.calloutText: A live demonstration of how Jana Earth Data powers a Nepali bank's commercial loan book against NRB's three regulatory frameworks.
steps.narration: Welcome. What you're looking at is a financed-emissions dashboard for First Bank of Nepal — a hypothetical Class A commercial bank with an 80,000-loan portfolio. Everything you see is wired to real Climate TRACE and EDGAR data from Jana Earth Data. Over the next three minutes I'll walk you through how a bank uses this to meet all three of Nepal Rastra Bank's environmental regulations through a single data platform.

steps.calloutText: ESRM screens new loans · Taxonomy classifies the book · NSRS produces annual disclosures.
steps.narration: The three tabs across the top map directly onto NRB's regulatory stack. ESRM, from the 2018 directive, is the credit decision layer — every new commercial loan gets screened for environmental risk before approval. Taxonomy, from October 2024, classifies your entire book as green, amber, or red. And NSRS, coming in 2026 and 27, requires public disclosure of financed emissions under the PCAF methodology. Most banks are stuck on all three because they don't have facility-level emissions data. Jana provides that data layer.

steps.calloutTitle: Small by count. Large by value. All the regulatory risk.
steps.calloutText: Of 80,000 loans, around 2,000 are commercial-industrial. Of those, around 120 borrowers match a verified Climate TRACE facility — across cement, hydropower, hotels, logistics, waste, and large industrial.
steps.narration: Here's the picture that matters. Of First Bank's 80,000 loans, only about 2,000 are commercial or industrial — the rest are home mortgages and personal loans that aren't in scope for environmental disclosure. Of those 2,000, around 120 commercial borrowers map to a Climate TRACE facility with verified satellite emissions — and they span every emissions sector where commercial credit attaches, not just heavy industry. Cement, hydropower, hotels, logistics, waste utilities, large industrial. By count, that's a small slice. By outstanding value, it's the slice that carries almost all of the environmental risk a regulator examines.

steps.calloutTitle: Tier 1 — Screen new loans before approval
steps.calloutText: Every commercial loan application gets an environmental risk assessment using real facility data, not borrower self-reporting.
steps.narration: Let's start with a new credit application. This is what a compliance officer at First Bank sees when a commercial loan comes across their desk. Real applications, real borrowers — each one needs an environmental risk assessment filed with NRB before approval. Without Jana, that's a manual research project per borrower. With Jana, it's a single API call.

steps.calloutTitle: Hongshi Shivam Cement — verified facility data
steps.calloutText: Real Climate TRACE 2024 emissions: 922,000 tonnes CO₂e. That's 4.9% of Nepal's national CO₂.
steps.narration: Let's drill into one borrower — Hongshi Shivam Cement, a Chinese-Nepali joint venture and the country's largest cement plant. The numbers you see here aren't estimates. The facility coordinates come from the Global Cement Tracker; the 922,000 tonnes of CO₂ comes from Climate TRACE satellite verification for 2024. The national-share metric — 4.9% — comes from EDGAR's polygon-clipped grid for Nepal. A single facility, attributable to a single loan, contributing nearly five percent of an entire country's carbon emissions. That's the kind of exposure a credit committee needs to see before they approve a 20 million dollar working capital line.

steps.calloutText: Coordinates match the GCCT registry. Verified by Climate TRACE assets. Auditable down to the dot.
steps.narration: This is the facility on a map. Coordinates from the Global Cement and Concrete Tracker, emissions from Climate TRACE's satellite data product, ownership from the Global Energy Monitor entity registry. Every number on this screen is sourced, citable, and reproducible. When NRB examines this loan three years from now, the bank can show exactly where the data came from.

steps.calloutText: PCAF-compliant Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions, ready for the annual report.
steps.narration: Fast-forward to the end of the year. First Bank needs to file its annual sustainability report under NSRS — Nepal's IFRS S2-aligned disclosure framework. This is the dashboard the CFO and CRO see. Total financed emissions across the book, with the most recent fully-reported year, and a multi-year trend. The number on the page is what goes into the annual report, with full PCAF methodology attribution underneath.

steps.calloutTitle: PCAF data quality — the technical moat
steps.calloutText: Without Jana: Score 5 across the board. With Jana: Score 2 on the slice that matters.
steps.narration: And here's the technical differentiator. PCAF requires every bank to disclose a data quality score from 1 to 5, with 1 being best. Without facility-level data, a bank defaults to Score 5 — revenue-based estimates using national averages. With Jana, the highest-emission slice of the portfolio moves to Score 2 — satellite-verified facility data plus public financial filings. NRB examiners and IFRS S2 auditors both look at this score. Jana moves the needle on the loans that matter.

steps.calloutTitle: One API. Three regulations. Full attribution.
steps.calloutText: Real Climate TRACE. Real EDGAR. Real GCCT. Climbing the PCAF score on the slice that carries the risk.
steps.narration: What you've just seen is one integration that handles all three of NRB's regulatory layers — credit screening, portfolio classification, and annual disclosure — using independent, satellite-verified data sources.
